hovi_playground_pid_mdoc.notes: Minted through the playground's (playground.hovi.id) Supabase edge function issue-credential, which answers without any key. The playground's page also sends Supabase's public anon key; it is not used here. credentialType is the playground's own name for the configuration; the sessionId must be new on every call. Photo ID, Age Verification, Health ID and LPID are in the metadata too, but their credentialType names are only listed in a table the anon key guards, so they have no row yet.

multipaz_pid_mdoc.notes: The token endpoint authenticates the client (token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: private_key_jwt, attest_jwt_client_auth); a token request without one fails 'client_id parameter missing' / 'clientId must be authenticated'. Only a wallet that presents a client or wallet attestation Multipaz accepts gets past it. Past the token endpoint, the configuration accepts only key-attestation proofs (proof_types_supported: attestation), not jwt proofs, so a wallet without key attestation also fails at the credential request. Expect this row to fail for wallets that support neither; it is kept to show when they do.

lissi_pid_sdjwt.notes: Lissi's own demo PID: its vct is not one of the listed credential types. It pairs only with the other lissi_pid_sdjwt row, and only in a wallet that accepts a vc+sd-jwt credential for a dc+sd-jwt request: the vct and claims match, the format identifiers do not. Minted the way www.lissi.id/demo-receive-pid does. The backend answers with a link into Lissi's own web wallet (https://wallet.lissi.io/lite?credential_offer_uri=…), so rewrite_scheme turns it into an openid-credential-offer:// link with the same query. The configuration's format is the older vc+sd-jwt identifier, while Lissi's verifier asks for dc+sd-jwt. Its authorization server lists only attest_jwt_client_auth as a token endpoint auth method while also allowing anonymous pre-authorized access; whether a wallet without an attestation is refused is unverified.

findynet_ips.notes: Minted through ips.digicredential.eu, the IPS demo deployment that issues from this issuer, with the sample bundle its own page uses (ips-demo.trustregistry.eu runs the same demo against a different Procivis issuer, …/7942c687…/beda035b…). The vct carries a .json suffix, as the metadata has it. Procivis serves issuer metadata only at the RFC 8615 path-inserted location and only with Accept: application/json (406 otherwise).

opintotodiste_student_status_sdjwt.notes: Minted through the opintotodiste.findy.fi demo: the setup step POST /demo loads the sample student's Koski records into a cookie session, then POST /credentials/<ref>/offer mints a pre-authorized offer (no tx_code, 600 s, single use) for one record. The ref is the demo's student-status record; refs were the same across demo sessions on 2026-11-15, and a stale one fails 404 'Todistetta ei löytynyt'. The token endpoint allows anonymous pre-authorized access (token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: none). The issuer also lists an ldp_vc OpenBadgeCredential configuration, which the demo never offers.

opintotodiste_openbadge_sdjwt.notes: Same demo flow as opintotodiste_student_status_sdjwt. The ref is the sample student's Matriculation Examination record; every record other than the student status is offered as OpenBadgeCredentialSdJwtVc.

eudiplo_pid_mdoc.notes: The parcel-pickup use case asks for given_name and family_name from either a PID mDoc (eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1) or a German SD-JWT PID (urn:eudi:pid:de:1); only the mDoc option is one of the credential types issued here.

igrant_playground_pid_mdoc.notes: by_reference.uri, not by_value: the by-value link carries an unsigned request under an x509_hash client id, which a wallet should reject.

igrant_playground_pid_sdjwt.notes: by_reference.uri, not by_value: the by-value link carries an unsigned request under an x509_hash client id, which a wallet should reject.

lissi_pid_sdjwt.notes: Lissi's own demo PID: its vct is not one of the listed credential types. It pairs only with the other lissi_pid_sdjwt row, and only in a wallet that accepts a vc+sd-jwt credential for a dc+sd-jwt request: the vct and claims match, the format identifiers do not. The www.lissi.id/demo-bank-verification use case, asking for given_name, family_name, birthdate and four address claims. The backend answers with a link into Lissi's own web wallet (https://wallet.lissi.io/lite?client_id=…&request_uri=…&request_uri_method=post), so rewrite_scheme turns it into an openid4vp:// link with the same query. Its request asks for format dc+sd-jwt, while the issuer row's configuration says vc+sd-jwt. The request is unsigned (alg none) under a redirect_uri: client id, which a strict wallet may refuse.

findynet_ips.notes: The verifier of the same IPS demo deployment (ips.digicredential.eu). Its request asks for the IPS vct with a single required claim, FullData, with holder binding; findynet_ips_issuer's configuration lists that claim, so the two pair. Its request is unsigned under a redirect_uri: client id, which a strict wallet may refuse, and the request object is served as header.payload without the trailing '.' an unsecured JWT needs (RFC 7519 section 6), so a strict JOSE parser may reject it before any consent screen.
